identity.title: Retire the legacy Tauri and React app

context_capsule.purpose_for_a_reader_without_history: The legacy app/ tree (Tauri shell and React UI) is retired after its remaining features have native owners and WP-KERNEL-017 has finished its notes-editor removal, with an Operator-approved list and an archive.

closure_unit.outcome: The legacy app/ tree (Tauri shell and React UI) is retired after its remaining features have native owners and WP-KERNEL-017 has finished its notes-editor removal, with an Operator-approved list and an archive.

materialized_acceptance.text: Feature and test census: every screen, command, shortcut, setting, e2e and unit test in app/ (475 tracked files: 142 components, 121 lib, 15 harness, Tauri shell) maps to a native owner with proof, to the WP-KERNEL-017 removal it belongs to, or to an explicit Operator-approved drop. Nothing is dropped by default (Q8).

Boundary with WP-KERNEL-017: the notes-editor removal (app/src/lib/editor, app/src/lib/tiptap, their dependencies and IPC) stays with WP-KERNEL-017 MT-261..MT-264 and their GREEN gate; this MT does not duplicate, precede or weaken it.

External consumers are listed with a replacement: CI jobs (.github/workflows/ci.yml app lint, depcruise, test and audit), the Codex direct-fetch rule, the workspace scope-binder test naming app/src-tauri, justfile references and docs.
Design tokens are preserved: the native palette comment states its values came from app/src/App.css; the values live in the native token source with the comment updated and no visual change.
The retirement is reversible: last buildable commit and dependency lockfiles archived under the approved archive location; the removal list is approved by the Operator in chat.
After removal the product builds, CI is green without app jobs, no product code or doc refers to a removed path except history, and the built-in manual no longer mentions it.
